MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 17, 2018

A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:03 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive
North, Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR RETZ.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR RETZ led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance

3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Pope, Portugal, Retz, Persichina,

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Romanelli, Wroan

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES, MAY 21, 2018

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  OF MAY 21, 2018 AS PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES, AUGUST 20, 2018

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  OF AUGUST 20, 2018 AS PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  COMMISSIONER ROLES DURING CITYWIDE DISASTERS

  Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst, provided information to the Park and Activities
  Commission regarding their roles in an event that there is a citywide disaster. Ms. Slawson stated
  that in an event of an emergency, the Park and Activities Commissioners are representatives of
  the city, the official roles have not been defined and staff is working on enhancing their emergency
  management program. One example of the items that will be addressed within the program is if
  the City Council does not have a quorum in making a decision, such as declaring a disaster to
  the state, then the city would have a stand-in policy. She recommended getting involved with
  CERT (Community Emergency Response Team), which is a volunteer program which educates
  on being personally prepared, aiding the community and family members.

  CHAIR RETZ asked if there will be any trainings at a future date. Ms. Slawson stated that there
  will be other dates. She will be meeting with Peninsula Emergency Preparedness group and will
  ask about future dates.

  COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL asked if the training being offered is specifically tailored for the
  Peninsula. Ms. Slawson stated that she believes so, but would need to confirm this with the
  coordinator.
  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if there is information on how many residents have gone through
  the training. Ms. Slawson stated that the city does not hold those records, they are held by LA
   County Fire and she will request a report from them.

  Community Services Director Clark asked about the shelter training. Ms. Slawson stated that this
  training is delivered by the Red Cross and will inquire about any opportunities for civilian staff.

B.  “BUTCHER PARK” REVISED CONCEPTUAL DESIGN

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the City Council has allocated a $100K budget for
  the design of the park. If everything is done as planned, the cost would be $347K. BMLA
  Landscape Architects developed a plan and came up with a budget of $99K with a contingency
  plan. The funding source is from Quimby funds that are coming from the Chadmar Development
  project.

  Community Services Director Clark recommended that another meeting be scheduled with the
  designer in order to get clarification on the revisions.

  CHAIR RETZ opened the public comment

  Sally Kensey, Palomino Ranchos HOA Resident, stated that she submitted questions on the cost
  estimates document to Community Services Director Clark. He will pass them on to the landscape
  architect.

  Ed Mohr, Montecillo Resident and HOA Secretary; stated that the cost estimate was revised and
  the site seems to be half the size of the original. He also noticed that five trees will be removed
  and wants to be sure that there is still shade. In addition there have been changes to the railing,
  monument sign, and seating. Mr. Mohr suggested purchasing seating at a lesser cost. He noticed
  that there is no longer a slide and there is now one swing versus two. Mr. Mohr also inquired
  about access from the end of Casaba or from the bridle trail. Community Services Director Clark
  stated that there will be access from the bridle trail. Mr. Mohr asked about parking on PVDE and
  stated that the east side says “NO PARKING” and that should be changed.

  Scott Combs, Montecillo Resident, expressed concern about the trees that will be removed, and
  wanted to make sure there will still be enough shade. He also stated that seating is necessary
  for people who are supervising their children.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there is a healthy tree maintenance budget which
  would include purchasing trees.

  COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL asked if the seating could be an Eagle Scout project. Community
  Services Director Clark stated yes, there are plenty of Eagle Scouts who would be able to help
  with this. He also mentioned that the seating is a very important element.

  Ms. Kensey suggested that long logs could be made to a comfortable height to be used for
  seating.

  Ryan McCormick inquired about the parks name and suggested that the city advertise for those
  interested in naming rights. Mr. McCormick also mentioned that fencing was an important element
  of the design and the revised plan shows that it is scaled back. Mr. McCormick stated that the
  fence should be the last thing scaled back. Mr. McCormick suggested “web” looking swings, which
  could accommodate several children on one swing and would not take up too much space.

  Robin Brooks, Dapplegray Resident, expressed her concern about the 3-rail fence and about
  cutting back on the slide and swings. She stated that those are features kids expect as a basic
  element of a park.

  Tracy Smith, Montecillo Resident, stated that she has kids that will use the park and also wanted
  to express her concern with the fencing. She also added that safety barriers are important to
  prevent anyone from being hurt due to a potential car crash. Community Services Director Clark
  stated that the barriers are still part of the design. Ms. Smith also inquired about what the tot lot
  will involve and also mentioned that there are swings that are for both adults and small children.
  She would like to see the park have features that could be enjoyable by a wide-range of park
  visitors.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that residents should send photos to him of ideas and
  designs and he will communicate these to the designer. Community Services Director Clark also
  stated that due to the CalWater project, this project may be delayed.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there is the possibility to ask the City Council for
  more funding for this project. He recommended that this item be continued to the October 15,
  2018 Park and Activities Meeting.

Park & Activities Commission Minutes  2
September 17, 2018
   The Park and Activities Commissioner agreed.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

C.  PARADE MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief summary of the staff report and stated that
  this item was brought back for further explanation. This is Pageantry Productions’ 21st year
  coordinating this parade. They are asking for a cost of living increase and also an increase due
  to rising General Liability Insurance costs.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Park and Activities
  Commission make a recommendation to the City Council to approve the agreement and added
  that the agreement has already been reviewed by the City Attorney.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if this is the first increase requested in a while. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that the first increase was after five years for $500 and $250 every
  year for the last four years. This agreement would bring the cost to $9500. Their actual starting
  cost is $10K.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if they have looked into having other companies coordinate the
  parade. Community Services Director Clark stated that this has been explored but have found
  that other companies run mostly festivals and although say that they may coordinate a parade,
  when speaking to former clients, they were not happy. A lot of cities coordinate their own parade.
  This vendor has good contacts and know all the bands.

  COMMISSIONER POPE moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO ENTER INTO THE
  AGREEMENT WITH PAGEANTRY PRODUCTIONS TO PROVIDE PARAGE
  MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS ON
  DECEMBER 1, 2018.

  Ayes: Pope, Portugal, Retz, Persichina
  Noes:
  Absent: Romanelli, Wroan
  Abstain:

D.  POCKET PARK PROJECT

  Community Services Director stated that the Taber’s have increased the budget to $100K towards
  the design and development of the park. At the last review of the park plan, there was a desire to
  include native trees and have suggested Coastal Live Oaks and California Sycamore trees. In
  addition the trail will be wide enough for vehicle access, such as emergency or city vehicles.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that on the Taber’s property that he has asked to for a
  pipe that runs through his property to be redirected and will be done at his cost. In addition, the
  City Manager has suggested that this not be called a park. The Taber’s have decided on John
  and Lynn Taber Grove with part of a poem by Henry Wadsworth to be inscribed on a bronze
  plaque.

  CHAIR RETZ asked about the large Yucca Tree at the top of the hill with making the width of the
  trail 8 feet. Community Services Director Clark stated that the area around the tree will need to
  be filled or add a retaining wall.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA, seconded by COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO CITY COUNCIL TO: 1) NAME THE POCKET PARK,
  “JOHN AND LYNN TABER GROVE” AND INSCRIBE IT ON A BRONZE PLAQUE WITH
  THEIR REQUESTED POEM AT THEIR COST; 2) DIRECT STAFF AND WILLDAN
  ENGINEERING TO DETERMINE WHICH PROJECT TASKS WILL BE COMPLETED BY
  EACH ENTITY; AND 3) REVIEW AND APPROVE THE CONCEPTUAL PARK PLAN.

  Ayes: Pope, Portugal, Retz, Persichina
  Noes:
  Absent: Romanelli, Wroan
  Abstain:

8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

Park & Activities Commission Minutes  3
September 17, 2018
   None

B.  RACE SUBCOMMITTEE DEBRIEFING MEETING

  Community Services Director Clark provided an update regarding the Hills Are Alive race. He
  stated that there was an issue with two couples who went around the Botanic Gardens multiple
  times. In addition, there was a request to start the race at 7:00 a.m. due to the heat. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that it would be difficult to have the youth volunteers there earlier
  and this will be discussed at their next meeting. Sponsorship was up with three new sponsors,
  however, registration was a little low.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER POPE, Community Services Director Clark stated
  that the heat may have been a factor and he has also heard that local races in general have low
  registration.

C.  PARADE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE

  Community Services Director Clark asked for suggestions for a Grand Marshall.

D.  CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING MEETING UPDATE

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the date will be determined and asked for
  any feedback from the Commissioners who were in attendance.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that he did not hear an announcement for the start of the
  equestrian events. COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL concurred. Community Services Director
  Clark stated that he will note that a third speaker is needed to cover all areas.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that he also attended the Remember the Music Festival and it
  was a great event as well.

9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEM

A.  LETTER FROM FORMER RESIDENT

  Community Services Director Clark shared a nice letter received from a former resident regarding
  a trail near the Chadmar Development.

10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF SEPTEMBER 11, 2018

B.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF AUGUST 27, 2018
C.
  CHAIR RETZ received and filed Items 10-A and 10-B

11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None

12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR RETZ adjourned the meeting at 8:02 p.m. to the next regular Park & Activities Commission
  meeting of Monday, October 15, 2018 beginning at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling
  Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
  Administrative Assistant  City Clerk
